corrected_value.title: Can the REBT theory explain loneliness? Theoretical and clinical applications
corrected_value.authors: Hyland; McGinty; Karatzias; Murphy; Vallières; McHugh Power

decisions.quote:
Hyland, P., McGinty, G., Karatzias, T., Murphy, J., Vallières, F., & McHugh Power, J. (2019). Can
the REBT theory explain loneliness? Theoretical and clinical applications. Cognitive Behaviour
Therapy, 48(1), 39–51. https://doi.org/10.1080/16506073.2018.1475505
decisions.location: References, p. 17, lines 1442-1444 (and The current study, pp. 4-5, lines 229-252)
decisions.reason: Both the shipped record and blind target 0 identify the same tested original study by Hyland, McGinty, Karatzias, Murphy, Vallières, and McHugh Power (DOI 10.1080/16506073.2018.1475505, published online in 2018 and in print in 2019), whose REBT psychopathology and psychological health models of loneliness are directly re-tested by this paper. Hyland et al. (2014) is cited only as the source of the ABS2-AV measurement scale and is not a tested target.

decisions.quote:
Thus, this study replicated the findings
from Hyland et al. in more representative samples from the five loneliest English-speaking
countries. Our results confirm the findings from Hyland et al. and consequently offer greater
credence and external validity to the potential therapeutic use of REBT to reduce loneliness
in various populations.
decisions.location: Conclusions, p. 16, lines 1341-1345 (and Abstract, p. 1, lines 67-70; Discussion, p. 13, lines 1220-1222)
decisions.reason: The authors state an explicit overall verdict across the Abstract, Discussion, and Conclusions that their results replicated and confirmed Hyland et al.'s (2019) findings for both the REBT psychopathology and psychological health models. Under Codebook Rule 1, this explicit overall replication verdict governs the paper-level outcome for this original despite a single pathway difference (a significant direct path from low frustration tolerance to loneliness in the psychopathology model) and country-level structural weight comparisons examined in the extension RQ1.

decisions.quote:
This
paper replicates the Hyland et al. analyses using a larger (N = 3,064)
sample drawn from the United States, United Kingdom, Canada,
Australia, and South Africa. The present results replicate Hyland
et al.’s results for both the psychopathology and psychological
health models, with minimal variation in model fit from country to
country.
decisions.reason: The study collected new survey data (N = 3,064 across five countries) to re-test the structural equation models of REBT beliefs and loneliness originally reported by Hyland et al. (2019), which makes it a replication under the codebook.
